preamble: Change of a palatalized voiced labial stop [bʲ] into a voiced palatal sibilant fricative. The labial closure is lost and the palatal element becomes a fricative, probably through an affricate stage. In Dzala (Dakpa-Dzala branch of Bodish), Proto-Bodish *bʲ appears as ཞ zh-, while the East Bodish languages Kurtöp and Khengkha have the affricate ཇ j-, and Dakpa has /tɕ/. The Tibetan letter ཞ is [ʑ] in Dzongkha, but published Dzala descriptions list the fricative as [ʒ]; ʑ and ʒ do not contrast in Dzala, so the exact place is not settled. In the Kurp dialect of Polish, by contrast, /bʲ/ gains a palatal sibilant but keeps the labial ([bʑ]), so it is not a case of this change.
phoneticEffects: Spirantization, Palatalization, Loss of Labial Articulation
